title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Discover the unique customs of Augustana University, from Scandinavian-inspired royalty to the legendary spirit of Ole the Viking.

cards.title: The Crowning of Royalty
cards.subtitle: A Century-Old Homecoming Tradition
cards.notes: Attend the official crowning of the Viking Days King and Queen in the Elmen Center, a tradition dating back to the first homecoming in 1924.
cards.short_summary: The central ceremony of homecoming week where student royalty is crowned.
cards.evidence_claim: Coronation is one of Augustana's longest-standing traditions, dating back to the first celebration in the early 1920s and held in the Elmen Center.
cards.access_notes: Held annually during Viking Days (homecoming) week in the Elmen Center.

cards.title: The Royal Knitwear
cards.subtitle: Scandinavian Heritage on Display
cards.notes: Watch for Viking Days royalty candidates wearing traditional Norwegian sweaters, a unique nod to the university's Lutheran Scandinavian roots.
cards.short_summary: Homecoming royalty candidates wear traditional Norwegian sweaters instead of formal attire.
cards.evidence_claim: Students nominated for Viking Days king and queen don Norwegian sweaters, a tradition reflecting the school's Scandinavian heritage.
cards.source_title: A Beardless Hobo & Other Homecoming Traditions
cards.access_notes: Visible during Viking Days parade and coronation events.

cards.title: The Spirit of Ole
cards.subtitle: Guardian of the Campus Green
cards.notes: Visit the concrete statue of Ole, designed by Peter Eide '66, which has stood guard over the campus quad since its dedication in 1967.
cards.short_summary: A landmark statue representing the university's mascot and Scandinavian identity.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ole the Viking statue was designed by Peter Eide '66 and has kept watch over the Augustana campus since 1967.
cards.access_notes: Located outdoors between the Administration Building and Morrison Commons; accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Viking Varieties Show
cards.subtitle: Student Talent Extravaganza
cards.notes: Experience one of AU's most beloved traditions, a student-led variety show featuring music, dance, and comedy during homecoming week.
cards.short_summary: A long-running talent show that serves as a highlight of the Viking Days celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Viking Varieties is one of Augustana's most beloved homecoming traditions, with its first show held in the gym.
cards.access_notes: Performances typically held in the Elmen Center during Viking Days.

cards.title: Christmas Vespers
cards.subtitle: A Sermon in Song
cards.notes: Join the community for this 80+ year tradition of music and word, featuring the Augustana Choir and multiple instrumental ensembles.
cards.short_summary: An annual holiday concert series that has been a campus staple since 1938.
cards.evidence_claim: The first Christmas Vespers service at Augustana was created in 1938 and has continued as an annual highlight.
cards.access_notes: Currently held at Gloria Dei Lutheran Church in Sioux Falls during early December.

cards.title: Festival of Sankta Lucia
cards.subtitle: Swedish Celebration of Light
cards.notes: Celebrate the Swedish 'Festival of Light' with a candlelit procession and traditional carols led by a student portraying Sankta Lucia.
cards.short_summary: A traditional Swedish holiday event honoring the university's cultural heritage.
cards.evidence_claim: The Festival of Sankta Lucia is a cherished holiday tradition that pays homage to the college's Swedish cultural heritage.
cards.access_notes: Held annually in early December, typically in the Chapel of Reconciliation.

cards.title: The Boe Forum
cards.subtitle: Global Voices in Sioux Falls
cards.notes: Attend this premier lecture series that has hosted world leaders like Mikhail Gorbachev and Condoleezza Rice since its inception in 1995.
cards.short_summary: A prestigious annual forum bringing global figures to campus for public discourse.
cards.evidence_claim: In 1995, the Center for Western Studies introduced the Boe Forum on Public Affairs, hosting many of the world's most influential leaders.
cards.source_title: Boe Forum on Public Affairs - Augustana University
cards.access_notes: Typically held in the Elmen Center; tickets are required but often free to the public.

cards.title: Sailing Into Service
cards.subtitle: Homecoming Community Impact
cards.notes: Participate in this Viking Days volunteer event where students create items for local charities, such as handmade toys for animal shelters.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated day of community service integrated into the homecoming week festivities.
cards.evidence_claim: Sailing Into Service is a Viking Days tradition where students give back to the community through various service projects.
cards.access_notes: Held on the Tuesday of Viking Days week, usually in the Morrison Commons.

cards.title: Augustana Twilight
cards.subtitle: Racing Under the Lights
cards.notes: Join thousands of fans for this massive night-time cross country race at Yankton Trail Park, featuring high school and collegiate divisions.
cards.short_summary: One of the largest night-time cross country meets in the region, hosted by AU.
cards.evidence_claim: The Augustana Twilight is one of the largest races in the region, attracting more than 5,000 participants and fans for races under the lights.
cards.source_title: Twelfth Annual Augustana Twilight Set for Sept. 1
cards.access_notes: Held annually in early September at Yankton Trail Park.

cards.title: The Viking Feast
cards.subtitle: A Community Meal with the Augie Bowl
cards.notes: Enjoy a community meal during Viking Days featuring the 'Augie Bowl' and live music from the Augustana Jazz Band.
cards.short_summary: A traditional homecoming meal that brings together students, staff, and retirees.
cards.evidence_claim: The Viking Feast is a long-held Viking Days tradition of enjoying a meal together, complete with the Augie Bowl.
cards.access_notes: Held on the Wednesday evening of Viking Days in the Elmen Center.
